memory_candidates: CSLib Labelled soundness: NIK.efq/NIK.orE (Deduction.lean) are cross-label rules whose conclusion label is fully independent of the premise label. Under CSLib's Wijesekera-style CKForces/CKValidFC semantics (per-world botForces, not Simpson's bivalent semantics), a naive 'generalize the soundness induction over an arbitrary interpretation ρ' motive is mathematically FALSE for these two constructors: botForces need not propagate to an r/≤-disconnected world. Machine-verified via a two-point countermodel (World := Pt one|two, ≤:=Eq, r:=Eq). Any future general soundness proof for this labelled system must either (a) prove a connectivity lemma that IsDerivationForest-built-from-Graph.trivial-via-addEdge implies TClosure-totality on G.X, or (b) use an existential-motive reformulation (∃ρ' agreeing with ρ on G.X∪ctxLabels Γ). The one-point model trick (World := Unit) used elsewhere in this file masks this issue rather than resolving it, since every map into Unit is trivially constant.
